thread:
Alex Kim: Hey team — we need a storage burst/reserve increase in eu-west-1 to support the new GPU training nodes landing next week. Current gp3 volumes hit baseline IOPS and snapshot jobs are queuing. Can we request both higher baseline IOPS per volume and a bump in concurrent snapshot jobs for the account?
Maria Chen: Thanks Alex — do you have numbers (volumes, IOPS per node, #nodes)? Also which project/account is this under? @quota-bot can you flag the support playbook? :eyes:
Alex Kim: Sure — planning for 40 p4d-like instances initially. Each instance attaches 4 x gp3 2TB volumes, expected sustained IOPS ~6000 per volume during checkpointing windows. Snapshot cadence: about 1 snapshot per volume every 6 hours. So we need snapshot concurrency from current 20 -> ~200 to avoid backlog. Account: redwood-eu-prod-02.
Sam Patel: Oof those IOPS numbers are high. Are these sustained or just bursts during checkpoints? Can we smooth with staggered snapshots or use incremental checkpoints?
Nora Ruiz: We did some tests on staging — it's bursty but concentrated in a 15-30m window per job. Staggering helps but complicates orchestrator. Also incremental snapshots still hit throughput limits because we write large checkpoints before the snap. Estimate peak account-level gp3 IOPS need around 3.2M IOPS total during peaks.
Maria Chen: Filing cloud support ticket now. Alex, please paste one sample aws cli command showing current quota and a quick justification blob we can copy into the ticket.
Alex Kim: Here's what I ran locally:```
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-7A4B22F8 --region eu-west-1
# current: 20 snapshot concurrency
```Justification: "Redwood inference dedicated training fleet launch requires increased EBS snapshot concurrency and baseline gp3 IOPS to prevent checkpoint backlog and meet SLOs for model training turnaround. 40 high-memory GPU nodes x 4 volumes/node with sustained checkpoint IOPS."
quota-bot: Support playbook: https://redwood.internal/cloud-playbooks/ebs-iops-snapshots. Created ticket CS-78912 and pinged AWS support with priority: high.
Sam Patel: Can we include a cost estimate so finance is aware? Rough calc: extra provisioned IOPS and snapshot throughput — Nora, any back-of-envelope?
Nora Ruiz: If we request baseline IOPS bump vs relying on burst credits, we'll pay additional gp3 provisioned IOPS. Rough monthly: extra 3.2M IOPS-seconds across peaks => ~€5k-7k/mo in provisioned IOPS, snapshots retention/egress another ~€2k/mo. Might be lower if we implement staged checkpoint windows.
Alex Kim: Good to know. For ticket: request increase to baseline gp3 IOPS quota for eu-west-1 to support 4 volumes x 40 nodes @ 6k IOPS each and snapshot concurrency -> 200. Mention ability to rollback if AWS suggests alternatives (throughput optimization, larger aggregate volumes).
Maria Chen: Ticket updated with numbers and cost note. AWS replied with initial ask for architecture diagram and justification — dropping that now.
Alex Kim: Pasting quick diagram link: https://redwood.internal/diagrams/gpu-fleet-checkpointing.png
Sam Patel: Can we also ask for temporary quota increase (30 days) while we implement staging improvements? That usually goes faster.
Maria Chen: Good call. Added temporary 30d surge request plus long-term quota increase in CS-78912.
quota-bot: AWS responded: asking for account-level snapshot throughput metrics and recent CloudWatch graphs. Maria/Nora, please attach the CW metrics to the ticket.
Nora Ruiz: Attached graphs (checkpoint_write_bytes/sec and snapshot_count) and a short note on mitigation plan (staggering, checkpoint compression).
Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. Once AWS approves the temporary bump we'll schedule onboarding of the first tranche of nodes. Will follow up with any rollback/runbook steps. :shipit:
